# Media fixtures

`sample-20s.webm` (74 kB) is generated by `build.mjs` and committed, like the `.pdf`, `.epub`
and `.pptx` fixtures beside it. Twenty seconds, 320×240, VP9 video and Opus audio.

Its audio is **`samples/jfk.wav` from [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp)**
(MIT-licensed repository), padded from eleven seconds to twenty. The recording itself is John
F. Kennedy's 1961 inaugural address — a work of the United States federal government, and
therefore in the public domain in the US under 17 U.S.C. §105. It is reused rather than
synthesised because the pipeline's acceptance criterion is a *transcript*, and a tone or a
silence produces none.

Its video is three flat colour fields with a caption on each, cutting at 0, 7 and 14 seconds,
so the keyframe pass has real scene changes to find and the OCR seam has real text to read.

VP9 and Opus, not H.264 and AAC, because the LGPL ffmpeg build the app ships carries no x264
(that is GPL) — so this is a format the shipped toolchain can both read and write, and one
Chromium plays natively.

Regenerate with:

```
pnpm sidecars:install                                  # fetches ffmpeg and jfk.wav
node packages/ingest/test/fixtures/media/build.mjs
```

The tests read the committed `.webm`; they never run this script.

A regenerated file is equivalent but **not byte-identical** — VP9 encoding is not
deterministic across runs — so re-running the builder produces a diff even when nothing
changed. Regenerate it only when the fixture actually needs to change.
